cards.text: Jehoiada the priest has died at 130 and been buried with the kings. Now the officials of Judah come and pay homage to Joash, king of Judah. Friend, the only thing that ever bowed to me in that junk drawer was an expired coupon somebody folded in half.

cards.question: With Jehoiada gone, the officials of Judah are bowing to King Joash. What does Joash do?

answers.text: He calls the priests in first

cards.question: Once King Joash starts listening to Judah's officials, they stay faithful to the house of the LORD.

cards.text: They abandon the house of the LORD, the God of their fathers, and serve Asherah poles and idols. Friend, that's walking out of a WARM bakery to go hug a cold fencepost.

cards.question: Wrath comes upon Judah and Jerusalem. What does the text say it comes for?

answers.text: Their failure to pay the temple tax
Their treaty with the king of Egypt

cards.text: But the LORD doesn't give up on them. He sends prophets to bring the people back to Him and to testify against them.

cards.question: The LORD sends prophets to bring His people back. How do the people respond?

answers.text: They ask the prophets for a sign

cards.text: Prophet after prophet, and the phone stays on SILENT. Then the Spirit of God comes upon a man named Zechariah, and he stands up before the people.

cards.question: Zechariah, the man the Spirit of God comes upon, is the son of ___ the priest.

cards.text: Zechariah brings them God's message: "Why do you transgress the commandments of the LORD so that you cannot prosper?"

cards.question: In God's message through Zechariah, the people have forsaken the LORD. What has the LORD done in return?

answers.text: He has sent them a new king

cards.text: Friend, this is where the story turns cold. They conspire against Zechariah.

cards.question: Zechariah's attackers stone him on their own, with no order from King Joash.
Where do they stone Zechariah, son of Jehoiada?

answers.text: In the courtyard of the house of the LORD
Outside the gate of the city
In the square by the king's palace

cards.question: When King Joash has Zechariah killed, he remembers the kindness Zechariah's father Jehoiada showed him.

cards.text: Instead, Joash kills Jehoiada's son. And as Zechariah lies dying, he speaks one last time.

cards.question: What does Zechariah say as he lies dying?

answers.text: May the LORD see this and call you to account
May the LORD forgive you for what you have done
May the LORD remember my father's house

cards.text: In the spring, the army of Aram goes to war against Joash. They march right into Judah and Jerusalem.

cards.question: The army of Aram enters Judah and Jerusalem. Who do they destroy?

answers.text: All the leaders of the people

cards.text: They send all the plunder home to their king in Damascus. Now wait till you hear how many men Aram brought to do all that.

cards.question: Aram comes with only a few men. Judah has a very great army. What happens?

answers.text: The LORD hands Judah's army to Aram
Judah's great army drives Aram out
The two armies agree to make peace

cards.text: A FEW men take down a VERY GREAT army. That's three guys winning tug-of-war against a whole stadium.

cards.question: Judgment comes on Joash because Judah had ___ the LORD, the God of their fathers.

cards.text: When the Arameans pull out, they leave Joash severely wounded.

cards.question: King Joash is lying severely wounded. Who conspires against him?
Why do Joash's servants conspire against him?

answers.text: For shedding the blood of Jehoiada's son
For losing the war against Aram
For taxing the people to repair the temple

cards.text: They kill Joash on his bed. He dies and is buried in the City of David.

cards.question: Joash is buried in the tombs of the kings, just like Jehoiada the priest.

cards.text: The men who conspired against him are named: Zabad and Jehozabad. More about Joash is written in the Treatise of the Book of the Kings, and his son Amaziah reigns in his place.

findings.problem: The question "What does the text say it comes for?" reads like a test question about the text. It doesn't sound like Papa Dorin pausing mid-story.

rule.text: Ask from inside the passage, the way a storyteller pauses to let the listener lean in. The question comes out of the moment Papa Dorin just set up.

findings.problem: Cards 2 and 3 already tell that Aram destroyed all the leaders and sent all the plunder to Damascus. Card 3 then hints at a small number of men. That setup rules out the wrong answers "Judah's great army drives Aram out" and "The two armies agree to make peace", so the right answer is given away.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: This story card only repeats what card 4 just revealed (a few men defeat a very great army), with a joke attached. It tells no new part of the passage, so it doesn't move the baker forward.

The wrong answers "honored" and "obeyed" are not believable reasons for judgment. A sentence saying judgment came because Judah had honored or obeyed the LORD makes no sense, so the card can be answered without thinking about the passage.

rule.text: For why and meaning questions, wrong answers only need to be believable.

findings.problem: This story card carries three beats: the conspirators are named, the records are in the Treatise of the Book of the Kings, and Amaziah reigns in Joash's place.

rule.text: Aim for one beat per story card. Two is the most. If a story card has more than two things happening, split it.

findings.problem: The joke makes up a new moment in the junk drawer: somebody folded the expired coupon in half. papa-dorin.md lets jokes "make up small moments and habits around his bakery" but also says he "never adds anything new" to his backstory. It doesn't say whether made-up moments in the drawer are allowed.
findings.question: Can Papa Dorin's jokes make up small moments in the junk drawer (like someone folding the coupon), or only around his bakery?
